title: Azure Bastion
learningObjective: Deploy Azure Bastion with the right SKU and subnet to give secure RDP and SSH access to VMs without public IPs.
foundation: Azure Bastion is a managed jump host: admins connect to VMs from the Azure portal (or a native client) over TLS, and the VMs don't need public IPs or open RDP/SSH ports to the internet.
engineer: SKUs: Developer (free, shared infrastructure, one connection at a time, no dedicated subnet, limited regions), Basic, Standard (native client support, shareable links, host scaling, IP-based connection, custom ports), Premium (adds session recording and private-only deployment).
Basic/Standard/Premium need a subnet named AzureBastionSubnet of /26 or larger and a Standard SKU public IP (except Premium private-only).
Bastion connects to VMs in its VNet and in peered VNets. VM NSGs must allow RDP/SSH from the AzureBastionSubnet address range; an NSG on AzureBastionSubnet itself needs specific required rules.
Native client: az network bastion rdp / az network bastion ssh (Standard or Premium, with Native client support enabled).
Pricing is hourly per deployment plus outbound data; scale units on Standard/Premium add hourly cost.

example.title: Removing public IPs from admin access
body: Contoso deploys Standard Bastion in the hub VNet, removes all VM public IPs and lets admins connect from the portal or with az network bastion ssh from their laptops.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription and a resource group (rg-net)
permissions: Network Contributor on the resource group
limits: Native client and shareable links need Standard or Premium
portal: Create a resource > Bastion: choose tier, VNet, new Standard public IP.
VM > Connect > Bastion: enter credentials (or a Key Vault secret).
configuration.cli:
az network vnet subnet create -g rg-net --vnet-name vnet-hub -n AzureBastionSubnet --address-prefixes 10.0.254.0/26
az network public-ip create -g rg-net -n pip-bastion --sku Standard
az network bastion create -g rg-net -n bas-hub --vnet-name vnet-hub --public-ip-address pip-bastion --sku Standard --enable-tunneling true
az network bastion ssh -g rg-net -n bas-hub --target-resource-id <vm-id> --auth-type AAD
configuration.powershell:
$vnet = Get-AzVirtualNetwork -Name vnet-hub -ResourceGroupName rg-net
Add-AzVirtualNetworkSubnetConfig -Name AzureBastionSubnet -VirtualNetwork $vnet -AddressPrefix 10.0.254.0/26 | Set-AzVirtualNetwork
$pip = New-AzPublicIpAddress -ResourceGroupName rg-net -Name pip-bastion -Location eastus -AllocationMethod Static -Sku Standard
New-AzBastion -ResourceGroupName rg-net -Name bas-hub -PublicIpAddressRgName rg-net -PublicIpAddressName pip-bastion -VirtualNetworkRgName rg-net -VirtualNetworkName vnet-hub -Sku Standard

misconceptions.myth: VMs need public IPs to use Bastion.

walkthrough.subtitle: Connect to VMs with RDP or SSH from the browser, without giving them public IPs.
learn: Why not open RDP/SSH to the internet

steps.label: Exposed
steps.title: RDP open to the world
body: Opening RDP or SSH on a public IP invites password-guessing attacks around the clock.

steps.label: Bastion
steps.title: Bastion is a managed jump box
body: Azure Bastion runs in your VNet. You open the portal, select Connect > Bastion, and get an RDP or SSH session in the browser over TLS (port 443). The VMs need only private IPs.

steps.label: SKUs
steps.title: Bastion SKUs
body: Developer: free, shared, one VM connection at a time, for dev and test. Basic: dedicated host. Standard: adds native client (connect from your own RDP/SSH app), shareable links, host scaling, IP-based connection. Premium: adds session recording and private-only deployment.

callout.text: Native client support requires Standard or Premium.

steps.label: Network
steps.title: What Bastion needs
body: Basic and higher need a subnet named exactly AzureBastionSubnet, size /26 or larger, and a Standard public IP (except private-only Premium). The target VMs' NSGs must allow RDP/SSH from the Bastion subnet.

callout.text: Wrong subnet name or a subnet smaller than /26 = deployment fails.

steps.label: Recap
steps.title: Bastion
body: Browser RDP/SSH, no public IPs on VMs.
recap: No RDP/SSH exposed to the internet
Sessions over HTTPS 443 in the browser
VM NSGs must allow from the Bastion subnet

handsOn.title: Connect to a VM with no public IP through Bastion
handsOn.cost: Low. One B1s VM costs about US$0.01 per hour. Delete the same day. Bastion Developer is free where offered; otherwise Basic costs about US$0.19 per hour, so delete it straight after.
before: Signed in at portal.azure.com as Owner of a subscription (a free or pay-as-you-go account works). Work in a resource group called rg-az104-lab.
If rg-az104-lab does not exist yet: search 'Resource groups' > Create > name rg-az104-lab, region UAE North (or any region near you) > Review + create > Create.

A virtual network vnet-lab (10.10.0.0/16) in rg-az104-lab with a subnet snet-app (10.10.1.0/24): Virtual networks > + Create > IP addresses tab. For these labs, untick 'Enable private subnet' on snet-app so lab VMs can reach the internet (in production use a NAT gateway instead).

A small Linux VM vm-lab in snet-app of vnet-lab: Virtual machines > + Create. Image Ubuntu 24.04, size Standard_B1s, password authentication, Networking tab: vnet-lab / snet-app, public IP: None, NIC network security group: Basic, public inbound ports: None. If the VM cannot reach the internet later, its subnet is private (the default for new networks): open the virtual network > Subnets, untick 'Enable private subnet', save, then stop and start the VM. In production use a NAT gateway instead.

steps.do: Open vm-lab > Connect > Connect via Bastion (or Bastion in the menu).
steps.see: Options to deploy Bastion. If 'Deploy Bastion Developer' is offered, choose it (free, no extra subnet).

steps.do: If Developer is not offered: open vnet-lab > Subnets > + Subnet, purpose Azure Bastion (name AzureBastionSubnet), range 10.10.3.0/26. Then deploy Bastion Basic from the VM's Bastion page.
When Bastion is ready, enter azureuser and the VM's password, and Connect.
steps.see: A new browser tab with a Linux terminal on vm-lab.

steps.do: In that terminal type: hostname && ip addr
steps.see: The VM's name and its private IP 10.10.1.x. It has no public IP.

steps.do: Open the Bastion resource > Settings > Configuration.
steps.see: The tier and the features available, such as native client support and shareable link (Standard+).

check: You opened an SSH session to a VM that has no public IP.
cleanup: Delete the Bastion resource right away if it is Basic or higher (billed hourly).
When you finish for the day: Resource groups > rg-az104-lab > Delete resource group > type the name > Delete. This removes everything inside it.
